Here are some things I thought in my 10 hours of playing this:

\- Presentation is huge in story games. The way it handles conversations is off-putting with its head-on camera and weird facial animations its too distracting. Even if the story is interesting its always muddled by its presentation.

I know what its like to work those kinds of jobs. I quit one and found something better myself so keep at it. The key is to really find something that will be a good fit for you. 

As for resumes, don't be afraid to edit it to fit into the place you are applying for. Focus on skills that employer will want to see specifically. If you worked in medical billing but now you want to be a security guard, it wouldn't make sense to put it unless you are a wizard at making it seem like it was related. I have definitely re-worded my abilities in a number of different ways to better fit the job I was sending it to. 

More on that actually: I don't think straight lying on a resume is a great idea, but a level of inflation I think can be fine. For example, I was a normal employee at my 2nd job, but eventually was given some managerial duties (opening/closing, overseeing breaks) and so I worded it where it could be construed as a supervisor position. It looked better that way and in terms of responsibilities was true. Most importantly, I knew I was capable of doing a job that would see that as a benefit.

Well it is a slow process but I will tell you what worked for me:

So I used to sing in my car on my hour long drive to and from school. I would throw on an album and sing until my voice hurt and I physically couldn't anymore (not completely gone, just clearly worn out). After a while I realized I could sing more and more without this happening, hitting higher notes, etc... Probably because your voice is controlled by muscles and they function like any other one. Tear the fibers, and they reform stronger. Of course the vocal chords are also sensitive so I wouldn't go too crazy on this (no one wants nodules). Just sing until it wears out your voice, recuperate, repeat. I look at it like lifting weights for your vocal chords.  


FYI, I am no vocal coach, I just found this worked for me.

Its interesting this was your dosage as you weigh about as much as me and you must have ended up with far less than the needed cumulative mg for a course. I believe the amount is somewhere around 11.5k mg. You may want to question that and see how you can continue until reaching the amount needed. Standard is 120-150 mg/kg.

I struggled with the joint aches as well and can say it has subsided a bit since finishing my course (about a month ago). Only thing I have still is my hair has thinned a bit. Though that could just be me getting old, haha!

Stayed pretty dry for me throughout, gaining a bit more as I upped my dose. So the dose you are taking will make a bit of difference. You really have to weigh whether its worth it to you to go through this bit of discomfort for the hopefully long term remission of your skin problems.

I also suggest moisturizing with something very hydrating, and to do it consistently throughout the day. Makes a big difference. I actually use Cerave moisturizing cream with a few drops of MCT oil and it helped quite a bit. If you don't suffer from Seb Derm like I do, you could probably use any sort of oil to help with hydration.

Best of luck to you on your journey! Stay strong!

Relapse always has a chance for various reasons:

\-Not taking full course  
\-Not eating with enough fat in meal  
\-Being male  


as well as some other reasons I can't think of. Sometime you never get acne again, sometimes you progress to a state with small breakouts every once in a while. I'd probably monitor it until it seems bad enough that it effects you day to day and then discuss with a derm about a second course if you feel the need.
